findings.body: None of the 20 identity providers created in the loop are actually removed during test cleanup (the lookup for alias 'alias' resolves to a non-existent resource), leaving residual test data that can affect subsequent tests or realm state.
findings.failure_mode: Cleanup silently fails to remove the created test fixtures, causing test data leakage/isolation issues.
findings.impact: None of the 20 identity providers created in the loop are actually removed during test cleanup (the lookup for alias 'alias' resolves to a non-existent resource), leaving residual test data that can affect subsequent tests or realm state.
findings.root_cause: Hard-coded literal string 'alias' used instead of the dynamically constructed alias variable used at creation time.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the actual alias variable, e.g. testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove.
findings.title: Test cleanup targets wrong/non-existent alias 'alias' instead of the created idp alias (loop)
findings.trigger: testCacheIDPForLogin() runs the loop creating 20 IDPs with aliases 'idp-alias-0'..'idp-alias-19'; the cleanup lambda is registered against the literal alias 'alias' for every iteration instead of the actual per-iteration alias.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 381 verbatim shows `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` inside a loop that creates IDPs with aliases `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`. The literal string "alias" does not match any created IDP alias, so cleanup will fail to remove the 20 created IDPs.

pr.title: Add cache for IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin

raw_findings.body: Every call to remove() now incurs an extra delegate/DB round-trip (idpDelegate.getByAlias) even in the previously cache-hit path, adding unnecessary load/latency on identity-provider removal.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Redundant database access on a previously cache-optimized code path.
raw_findings.impact: Every call to remove() now incurs an extra delegate/DB round-trip (idpDelegate.getByAlias) even in the previously cache-hit path, adding unnecessary load/latency on identity-provider removal.
raw_findings.root_cause: The delegate lookup was hoisted above the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch to obtain data for the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation() call, without reusing the cached value already available in the else branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only call idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) when actually needed (e.g., reuse the already-fetched cached.getIdentityProvider() in the else branch, or lazily resolve storedIdp only for the login-invalidation check when it's not already available from cache).
raw_findings.title: Unconditional delegate lookup added to remove() even when cache entry is valid
raw_findings.trigger: remove(alias) is called while the alias cache entry is still valid (isInvalid(cacheKey) == false), a path that previously relied on realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class) instead of hitting the delegate.

raw_findings.body: Increased maintenance burden and risk of divergence/inconsistent bug fixes between the two structurally identical caching implementations.
raw_findings.evidence: public Stream<IdentityProviderModel> getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId) {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Code duplication leads to inconsistent maintenance and higher risk of divergent bugs in nearly identical caching code paths.
raw_findings.impact: Increased maintenance burden and risk of divergence/inconsistent bug fixes between the two structurally identical caching implementations.
raw_findings.root_cause: New getForLogin() method was implemented by copy-pasting the existing getByOrganization() caching pattern instead of factoring out common logic.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extract the shared query-list caching logic (lookup, stale-search-key handling, revalidation loop) into a private generic helper parameterized by cache key, search key, and the delegate-fetch supplier, and have both getByOrganization and getForLogin call it.
raw_findings.title: getForLogin() duplicates the entire caching algorithm already implemented in getByOrganization()
raw_findings.trigger: Any future change to the shared query-caching/invalidation algorithm (e.g., handling of stale cached IDs, revision tracking) must now be made in two nearly-identical ~35-line blocks (getByOrganization and getForLogin).
